title: Nuclear and SMR techno-economic parameters and inputs
description: Source-specific nuclear power and small modular reactor techno-economic parameters and inputs, preserving printed values, technical and monetary bases, source terms and paper cross-references. Includes reference-plant estimates, fleet observations, design descriptions, policy parameters and regulatory charges.
temporal_coverage_note: January 1986 decommissioning-assurance cost bases, 2020–2025 fleet observations, 2026 policy and regulatory records, 2030-onward reference scenarios and construction-start phaseout cases through 2036 onward.
spatial_coverage_note: United States focus; Canadian-filed vendor material is supplementary design context.
coverage_intro: United States focus; Canadian-filed vendor material is labeled as supplementary design context.
compilation_rights_note: Compilation and curation: CC BY 4.0. Each value retains the original source’s terms, listed in the source register; this compilation licence does not relicense source documents.
reading_conventions: Values retain their source-specific bases; costs have not been escalated or converted. NR means not reported or not established, never zero. FOAK means first-of-a-kind; BOAK means between first- and nth-of-a-kind; NOAK means nth-of-a-kind. Blank numeric fields are missing values. Suffixes separate scenarios or years while retaining the common N-number. Verification of a printed value does not establish realized cost, performance or eligibility.
paper_crosswalk_note: The paper column labels input use, citation provenance, numerical correspondence and contextual discussion separately. Input use identifies a stated model assumption; it does not establish the original source. Context is not a numerical input. Only examined public versions are linked, with version-specific locators. All expanded basis and locator text is present in the page and downloads.
verification_note: The nuclear CSV separately records transcription verification, underlying evidence, source conflicts and numerical-field interpretation. Source editions, revisions, release dates, publishers, retrieval dates and document SHA-256 values travel with each row. Semicolon-separated source IDs resolve to the accompanying JSON register; expanded bibliographic fields retain each source’s full text. NR denotes an unreported date or revision; it is not a date inferred from access. Document checksums identify source bytes, not independently validated engineering performance.
reuse_code_note: Reuse codes: G — government-authored material, subject to third-party exceptions; A — explicit attribution-based permission, retaining restrictions; C — conditional handling for contractor, mixed or vendor material, not a licence; ND — CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 on the identified article version.

definition_risks: Overnight versus total capital
Record IDC/AFUDC, escalation during construction, owner’s costs, contingency, initial fuel and interconnection separately. A table labelled “Total Capital Cost” may still be an overnight total.
FOAK versus BOAK versus NOAK
Preserve the source’s term. Distinguish first design, first country deployment, first site unit and repeat factory production.
$/kWe versus $/kWth
Never substitute one for the other without an explicit efficiency and boundary.
Net versus gross output
Record auxiliary demand and whether the denominator is generator output, plant export or delivered customer power.
Capacity factor versus availability
Fleet CF includes generation behavior; availability describes whether equipment can operate. Neither alone establishes data-center service reliability.
Ramp rate versus operating envelope
Identify rated-power denominator, electric versus thermal power, permitted range, time resolution and fuel-cycle conditions.
Design life versus licence term
Keep technical life, amortization life, analysis horizon and regulatory permission in separate fields.
Fuel price versus fuel cost
Uranium and SWU purchase prices do not determine $/MWh without enrichment, tails, fabrication, burnup, efficiency and inventory assumptions.
Production versus investment credit
§45Y applies to qualifying production; §48E applies to qualified investment. Percentage bonuses and percentage-point adders differ.
Reactor temperature versus usable heat
Include steam pressure, phase, extraction location, return conditions and temperature losses.
Footprint versus site
Separate building envelope, protected area, owner-controlled area, construction laydown, cooling systems and EPZ.
Vendor claim versus reviewed value
Government hosting does not make vendor content a government endorsement. Design approval does not establish commercial performance.
Decommissioning assurance versus expenditure
A regulatory minimum funding formula is not a complete project cost estimate.
Historical order versus current entitlement
A dated FERC order cannot establish today’s contractual limit without checking subsequent proceedings.
Verification and source conflicts

Transcription verification confirms what a document prints. The separate underlying-evidence and conflict fields describe the limits of that evidence. Neither a model input nor a vendor design claim is independently demonstrated operating performance.
Policy scope and payment

Qualifying capacity additions at older facilities can fall within §45Y/§48E. Domestic-content requirements can affect elective payment as well as bonus eligibility; statutory exceptions and waivers must be checked.
Source versions

Edition, revision, release date, retrieval date and document SHA-256 are separate fields. A checksum identifies retrieved bytes, not accuracy; live HTML navigation can change without changing a cited table.

gaps.title: ATB nuclear cost workbook
gaps.text: The narrative chapter is included; a cell-level cost export is still needed before adding ATB capital-cost records.

gaps.title: INL revision reconciliation
gaps.text: Internal capital, fuel and future-cost differences require comparison with subsequent revisions or errata.

gaps.title: Plant-specific flexibility
gaps.text: Public design- and fuel-cycle-specific operating constraints are needed for load following and ramp rates. Historical summaries do not establish licensed plant limits.

gaps.title: Licensing milestones
gaps.text: Licensing pathway and milestone definitions require separate evidence; executive deadlines do not establish observed approval duration.

gaps.title: All-in U.S. SMR capital cost
gaps.text: A consistently scoped commercial benchmark remains unavailable here. Financing, owner costs and shared-site allocation need explicit treatment.

gaps.title: Advanced-reactor operating costs
gaps.text: Technology-specific staffing, fuel cycles and maintenance need stronger public evidence; generic SMR estimates are not interchangeable across HTGR, SFR and MSR designs.

gaps.title: Delivered process heat
gaps.text: Pressure reference, return temperature, enthalpy states, delivery distance and extraction penalties remain necessary for a project heat balance.

gaps.title: Current complete-site footprints
gaps.text: Historical protected-area claims do not establish current application-specific total land, cooling or construction needs.

gaps.title: Decommissioning estimates
gaps.text: Site-specific expenditure estimates and advanced-reactor end-state assumptions are needed in addition to statutory financial assurance.

gaps.title: Current co-location arrangements
gaps.text: Later FERC orders, tariffs and agreements must be checked for a contemporary project; the November 2024 order is historical.
